title: Polynomial threshold function
statement: Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers, and let $f$ map the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube to the signs. Then $f$ is a polynomial threshold function of degree at most $k$ if there is a real-valued polynomial on the cube whose threshold sign agrees with $f$ at every input and whose Fourier degree is at most $k$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube to the signs
